samuel2.20.p1.b1.text: Now a worthless man named Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjamite, happened to be there, and he blew the ram’s horn …

samuel2.20.p1.b2.text: “We have no share in David, no inheritance in Jesse’s son. Every man to his tent, O Israel!”

samuel2.20.p1.b3.text: So all the men of Israel deserted David to follow Sheba son of Bichri.

samuel2.20.p1.b4.text: But the men of Judah stayed by their king all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

samuel2.20.p2.b1.text: When David returned to his palace in Jerusalem, …

samuel2.20.p2.b2.text: … he took the ten concubines he had left to care for the palace, and he placed them in a house under guard. He provided for them, but he no longer slept with them. They were confined until the day of their death, living as widows.

samuel2.20.p2.b3.text: “Summon the men of Judah to come to me within three days, and be here yourself.”

samuel2.20.p2.b4.text: So Amasa went to summon Judah, but he took longer than the time allotted him.

samuel2.20.p3.b1.text: “Now Sheba the son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom. Take your lord’s servants and pursue him, …”

samuel2.20.p3.b2.text: So Joab’s men, along with the Cherethites, the Pelethites, and all the mighty men, marched out of Jerusalem in pursuit of Sheba son of Bichri.

samuel2.20.p4.b1.text: And while they were at the great stone in Gibeon, Amasa joined them. … And as he stepped forward, he slipped the dagger from its sheath.

samuel2.20.p4.b3.text: Amasa was not on guard against the dagger in Joab’s hand, … And Joab did not need to strike him again, for Amasa was dead.

samuel2.20.p4.b4.text: Then Joab and his brother Abishai pursued Sheba son of Bichri.

samuel2.20.p5.b1.text: “Whoever favors Joab, and whoever is for David, let him follow Joab!”

samuel2.20.p5.b2.text: … when the man saw that all the troops were stopping there, he dragged the body off the road into a field and threw a garment over it.

samuel2.20.p5.b3.text: As soon as Amasa’s body was removed from the road, all the men went on with Joab to pursue Sheba son of Bichri.

samuel2.20.p5.b4.text: And Joab’s troops came and besieged Sheba in Abel-beth-maacah and built a siege ramp against the outer rampart of the city. As all the troops with Joab were battering the wall to topple it …

samuel2.20.p6.b1.text: “Listen! Listen! Please tell Joab to come here so that I may speak with him.”

samuel2.20.p6.b2.text: I am among the peaceable and faithful in Israel, but you are trying to destroy a city that is a mother in Israel. Why would you swallow up the LORD’s inheritance?”

samuel2.20.p6.b3.text: “Far be it from me to swallow up or destroy! … Deliver him alone, and I will depart from the city.”

samuel2.20.p6.b4.text: “Look,” … “his head will be thrown to you over the wall.”

samuel2.20.p7.b1.text: Then the woman went to all the people with her wise counsel, …

samuel2.20.p7.b2.text: … and they cut off the head of Sheba son of Bichri and threw it to Joab.

samuel2.20.p7.b3.text: So he blew the ram’s horn and his men dispersed from the city, each to his own home.

samuel2.20.p7.b4.text: Now Joab was over the whole army of Israel; Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and Pelethites; …
